askSize: If the user gave no size, do not ask: scan at the default size, 1,000 USD unless the user changed it. Name the size in the first sentence of the reply (`sizeUsd` in the result), and offer a re-rank at 5,000 or 25,000 USD in the closing You can.
askOwner: If owner is unset, ask: What is your public wallet address (it starts with 0x)? Never ask for a key. Wait for the address, then use it with `--owner`. Do not change config unless the user explicitly asks to save it.
askWallet: If owner is unset, ask: Which wallet do you want to use? Reply `browser` for a wallet extension (MetaMask, Rabby), `import` to bring your wallet into mstack's encrypted keystore, `create` for a new wallet made by mstack, or `phone` for WalletConnect (needs a free Reown project id). For `browser` or `phone`, ask for its public 0x address; for `phone`, the human gets a free project id at https://cloud.reown.com and saves it in their own terminal with `mob config set walletconnect_project_id` and the id. For `import` or `create`, the human runs `mob keystore import` or `mob keystore create` in a separate terminal window, never in this chat, and replies with the address it prints. A created wallet starts empty; its keystore file (`~/.mob/keystore` by default) and passphrase are the only copy: the human backs up both and funds the wallet on each venue. Never ask for or accept a private key, seed phrase, or passphrase in the chat. Pass the address with `--owner`; `mob onboard` saves it only once setup is staged.
askOpen: Ask for each missing choice in prose. Wait for the answer before staging.
askSign: Ask in prose, offering the way that fits the user's wallet, plus `reject <id>`: browser wallet, "Reply `sign <id>` to sign <id> in the browser wallet"; phone wallet, "Reply `sign <id> walletconnect` to sign with WalletConnect"; keystore wallet, "Reply `sign <id> approver` when your approver terminal is running, or run `mob sign <id> --with keystore` in your own terminal". The wallet comes from this conversation or `mob config get signer`; if neither says, offer every way. Put the staged id in place of <id>. Only a reply that says `sign <id>` authorizes. Run the matching command with a ten-minute tool timeout: `sign <id>` means `mob sign <id> --with browser`, `walletconnect` means `--with walletconnect`, and `approver` means `--with approver`.
askSubmit: Ask in prose: "Reply `submit <id>` to send it, or `reject <id>`." Replace <id> with the staged Proposal id. Only a reply that says `submit <id>` authorizes the submission.
askTrade: Trading runs through MoB with a scoped API key the user controls: it has venue and USD caps, cannot withdraw, and can be revoked at any time. Ask in prose: "Trading runs through MoB. Set it up now? One wallet session, about five minutes. Reply `set up` or `not now`." Ask only this and stop; add nothing after the question. Only after `set up`, load `$mob-setup` and follow it. After `not now`, offer a scan, funding history, or an explanation, and do not bring up setup again until the user asks to trade.
askMenu: list every entry of `sections` in `mob menu --json`, in order: its `name` and `note` as a heading, then its rows as numbered lines, numbering on across sections: the `say` words, then the `about`. Ask which number or words to run, then stop. When the chosen row has `pick`, ask which asset, naming the `assets` tickers (any ticker works), and put it in place of `<asset>` in `pick`. Treat the reply, a number or words, as the user's own request: load the skill for it and follow it.
